annotation.title_clean: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.title_en: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.venue: Innovation Journal of Social Sciences and Economic Review
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual journal article proposing a robot-first Mars settlement framework in which a swarm of about 10,000 autonomous AI robots prepares and tests infrastructure before humans arrive. It sets out governance implications: human oversight, accountability, planetary protection and compliance with international space law.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous robotic swarms could test energy systems, habitats and ways of recovering from failure on Mars before humans arrive.
Controlled failure by robots turns risk into operational learning and reduces uncertainty.
Robot-first colonization should add to human settlement, not replace it.
Governance of autonomous robotic colonies requires human oversight, accountability and planetary protection.
Robot settlement activities must comply with international space law.
